name: Vansen ArcWarm Heated Glove — Chrome-Socket Fit
description: Thick neoprene-shell gloves with embedded resistive heating wire and a reinforced chrome-socket palm that accommodates partial hand augmentations and wrist interface ports. The heating system is powered by a slim battery cell worn at the wrist, giving 8 hours of warmth at -30C. Available in black and gunmetal.
functionality: Active resistive heating rated to -30C wind chill; palm socket accommodates partial hand chrome and wrist interface hardware without pressure points.
what_it_says: Someone who invested in proper aug-compatible winter gear — not rich, but not cutting corners on their hands.
worn_by: small business owners with chrome hands
story_hooks: The battery cell has been modified to run hotter than spec — whoever did it knew exactly how close to the thermal limit they could push.
One glove's socket fit is calibrated for a rare discontinued chrome model; whoever owned these had very specific hardware.
